methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
1X Technologies, a Pre-Seed stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Bernt Øivind Børnich, operates within a fragmented comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). The broader sector encompasses 11 identifiable peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics, though meaningful median-based valuation anchoring is constrained by insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within narrow peer filters.

Given these data limitations, the Stage-Progression method represents the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($1.1B) as a proxy floor valuation of $2M and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Pre-Seed advancement, this method implies a valuation of $5M. The methodology assumes standard venture progression multiples hold despite the company's substantial prior fundraising.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M (median $5M), anchored primarily to stage-based progression mechanics rather than peer comparables. Key uncertainties include (1) the absence of a robust same-stage peer median to validate or adjust the 2.5x multiplier, (2) the relationship between cumulative capital raised and pre-money valuation given the company's atypical funding trajectory, and (3) sector-level performance heterogeneity in robotics valuations. This range should be treated as indicative pending access to transaction multiples within the narrower robotics manufacturing peer set.
